hook: SCP-5699 is a short, quiet entry about a figure that appears to people at their lowest point, including those thinking about or attempting suicide. Most of the article is a collection of messages left behind on mirrors, and they reward being read slowly, one at a time. Keep the footnotes in view; one of them changes how the ending lands.
whyItMatters: It turns the usual containment logic around. The procedures conclude that stopping this anomaly would take mass incarceration, city lockdowns and heavy amnestics, so the Foundation decides to leave it alone. Its tags file it under heartwarming and kindness, and it earns that through small, specific moments rather than grand miracles.
thingsToNotice:
The messages are written in the voice of the person being comforted and addressed to 'you', and in line with the description each one recalls an act of affection from the subject's own life. A badly made, half-spilled cup of tea brought to someone shivering in bed, a dress and the reassurance that the girl inside was finally free, a hug given when nobody else would risk it, a hand held through the last beeps of a hospital monitor. A few are told from outside, about an old woman at a hospital window or a man sleeping by the pub.

The addendum flips the direction. The message on Dr. Pearson's bathroom mirror thanks him for letting it out of its cell to wander and love, for doing what his name and position should have forbidden, and promises to free others in its own way. The footnote then reveals that Pearson, the project's research lead, suffers from severe depression, which makes him exactly the kind of person the entity visits.
